event: Solar system forms; CAIs condense as the first solids
notes: Date firm to +/- 0.16 Myr. Birth trigger contested: supernova vs Wolf-Rayet bubble vs ambient ISM inheritance. High 26Al with low 60Fe is the key tension.

event: Chondrules form over a 2-3 Myr window
notes: Iron meteorite parent bodies differentiate within ~1 Myr of CAIs.

event: Planetesimals form via streaming instability; pebble accretion builds giant planet cores
notes: Bypasses the meter-size barrier. Giant cores must form within the few-Myr gas disk lifetime.

event: Giant planet migration (Grand Tack); inner disk truncated
notes: Explains Mars's small mass and the asteroid belt's two source populations.

event: Theia impact forms the Moon
notes: Competing models: canonical (Canup & Asphaug 2001), fast-spinning Earth (Cuk & Stewart 2012), synestia (Lock & Stewart 2018), multiple impacts (Rufu 2017), immediate satellite (Kegerreis 2022). Isotopic similarity is the central problem.

event: Post-impact: global magma ocean; rock vapor atmosphere at 2300-3500 K
notes: Moon orbits at ~3-4 Earth radii. Day length ~5 hr (Touma & Wisdom) or under 2.5 hr with high obliquity (Cuk 2016).

event: LLVPs emplaced at the core-mantle boundary
notes: Yuan et al. 2023 proposes these are buried fragments of Theia's mantle. Alternatives: subducted crust or basal magma ocean cumulates.

event: First oceans; liquid water at the surface
notes: Jack Hills zircons: elevated delta-18O indicates low-temperature water interaction. The 'cool early Earth.'

event: Possible Late Heavy Bombardment
notes: May not have happened. Apollo sample ages may be an Imbrium ejecta artifact. Many now favor an early instability within ~100 Myr of formation.

event: Sun at 1 L-sun; Moon recedes 3.83 cm/yr; day lengthens 1.7-2.4 ms/century
notes: CO2 ~425 ppm. Obliquity stable at 23.3 +/- 1.3 degrees thanks to the Moon.

event: Next supercontinent assembles; lethal continental interior heat
notes: Four scenarios: Pangaea Ultima, Novopangaea, Aurica, Amasia. Farnsworth et al. 2023 projects 40-70 C interiors and near-total mammalian extinction. Only 8-16% of land stays survivable. Arrives ~4x sooner than the classic deadlines.

event: Day length reaches ~25 hours
notes: Tidal spin-down continues but decelerates asymptotically.

event: CO2 starvation; C3 then C4 photosynthesis fails
notes: C3 fails below ~150 ppm, C4 below ~10 ppm. Caldeira & Kasting 1992 give 0.9-1.5 Gyr; Lenton & von Bloh 0.8-1.2 Gyr; Franck ~500 Myr. The carbonate-silicate thermostat draws CO2 down as the Sun brightens.

event: Atmospheric oxygen collapses; ozone layer lost
notes: Ozaki & Reinhard 2021: 1.08 +/- 0.14 Gyr, over a ~10000 yr transition. Reverts to an Archean-like state. Precedes ocean loss.

event: Animals and most eukaryotes die out
notes: Heat, unshielded UV, and anoxia compound.

event: Earth enters chaotic obliquity regime
notes: As the Moon recedes, Earth's precession frequency drifts into secular spin-orbit resonances. Obliquity could wander 0-85 degrees (Laskar 1993). Lissauer 2012 argues this is less catastrophic than originally framed.

event: Moist/runaway greenhouse; oceans evaporate
notes: 1-D models (Kasting, Kopparapu 2013) say 0.65-1 Gyr. 3-D cloud models (Wolf & Toon 2015) say 1.5-2 Gyr. Leconte 2013 finds no distinct moist-greenhouse state at all. This is the single widest disagreement in the timeline.

event: Hypersaline seas, vast evaporite deposits, final brine refugia
notes: Last standing water is dense brine. Thermohalophile habitat.

event: Last deep-subsurface microbes die; biosphere ends
notes: Upper temperature limit for life is 122 C (Methanopyrus kandleri, Takai 2008). O'Malley-James puts detectable biosignatures ending at 2.0-2.8 Gyr.

event: Venus-like Earth: thick CO2 atmosphere, no oceans, baking crust
notes: Runaway greenhouse can drive surface temperatures toward 1500-1600 K in the extreme limit.

event: Mantle cooling ends plate tectonics; transition to stagnant lid
notes: Radiogenic heat from U, Th, K declines. Ends volcanic CO2 outgassing and the weathering thermostat.

event: Geodynamo weakens and ceases; magnetic shield lost
notes: Inner core growth eventually stops core convection. Timing highly uncertain. Accelerates atmospheric stripping.

event: Possible inner planet orbital destabilization
notes: ~1% of solutions in Laskar & Gastineau 2009 (2501 integrations). Mercury's eccentricity grows enough for collision with Venus or the Sun. Perturbing Mercury by 0.38 mm flips the outcome.

event: Core hydrogen exhausted; Sun leaves the main sequence
notes: Fusion moves to a shell around an inert contracting helium core.

event: Red giant branch ascent; ~0.6 Gyr climb
notes: Sun sheds up to ~28% of its mass. Planets drift outward as solar gravity weakens.

event: RGB tip: 2730 L-sun, 256 R-sun (1.2 AU), 2600 K surface
notes: Schroder & Smith 2008. Sun has lost 0.332 solar masses. Mercury and Venus engulfed.

event: Helium flash; degenerate core ignites
notes: Triple-alpha process begins. Degeneracy lifted. Mostly invisible from outside.

event: Earth engulfed (probably)
notes: Race between mass-loss orbital expansion and tidal drag. Schroder & Smith 2008 say engulfed; Nordhaus 2010 says survives with higher mass loss. If engulfed, Earth spirals to the core in ~3000 yr. If not, a bare molten or iron-rich remnant at ~1.4 AU.

event: Horizontal branch: core helium burning for ~100 Myr
notes: Sun contracts to a few tens of L-sun. The last quiet interval.

event: AGB: ~3000 L-sun, thermal pulses, dredge-up
notes: Brighter than the RGB tip and reached in ~20 Myr rather than 0.6 Gyr. Surface enriched in carbon, nitrogen, and s-process elements. Whether the Sun becomes a carbon star is at the edge of models.

event: Icy moon habitable window
notes: Titan: several hundred Myr of liquid water-ammonia (Lorenz 1997). Europa: ~0.2 Gyr vapor atmosphere (Mullens 2025). Stern's 'delayed gratification habitable zone.' Saturn's rings sublimate.

event: Planetary nebula ejected; visible ~10000 yr
notes: Exposed core at 100000-200000 K photoionizes the shell. Brief peak of several thousand L-sun.

event: White dwarf remains: ~0.5-0.55 solar masses
notes: Carbon-oxygen core, roughly Earth-sized. ~15 L-sun at peak, almost entirely extreme UV. Surviving planets' orbits have roughly doubled.

event: Oort cloud stripped; Kuiper belt stirred
notes: Solar mass loss plus galactic tides and stellar flybys (~20 encounters within 1 pc per Myr, Bailer-Jones 2017).

event: Milky Way-Andromeda merger
notes: Sawala et al. 2025 puts it near 50% within 10 Gyr. Wu et al. 2026 revises back to ~90%, median ~6.5 Gyr. Genuinely open.

event: White dwarf cooled to ~4000 K; 0.00004 L-sun
notes: A small orange star. Surviving planets frozen. Equivalent to sunlight at ~160 AU.

event: White dwarf core crystallizes; latent heat delays cooling
notes: Oxygen crystallizes first and sinks; carbon floats. Confirmed by Gaia as a pile-up in the cooling sequence.

event: White dwarf cools to a black dwarf
notes: ~1 million Gyr. No black dwarf exists yet anywhere; the universe is ~70000x too young.

event: Galaxies evaporate via stellar scattering
notes: Adams & Laughlin 1997.

event: Proton decay erodes remnants
notes: Never observed. A proton-decay-fueled white dwarf radiates ~400 W — an entire galaxy of them dimmer than one hydrogen-burning star.

event: Dark era: only low-energy photons and leptons
notes: Black holes evaporate via Hawking radiation by ~10^100 yr.
